Requirement: Book text is primary. Existing game bibles are secondary. New invention fills only gaps the book does not answer.
Implementation Note: When a detail conflicts, mark it rather than silently harmonizing it.

Requirement: Use exact names, single words, short address terms, and brief fragments only. Dialogue in the game must be newly written.
Implementation Note: No copied paragraphs, speeches, or recognizable scene transcripts.

Requirement: Keep columns for exact source name and working game analogue.
Implementation Note: Classroom prototype may show source names; commercial build requires rights/trademark review.

Requirement: Build speech from rhythm, grammar, subject matter, and avoidance patterns - not repeated quotations.
Implementation Note: Abel should sound like himself even when discussing a new event.

Requirement: Every nickname records who says it, whether it is private/public, affectionate/controlling, and how its meaning changed.
Implementation Note: A warm term can become unsafe; the game should remember context.

Requirement: Put history in jokes, errands, meals, and remembered objects instead of exposition dumps.
Implementation Note: A belt joke can conceal a burn story; a doughnut can signal town belonging.

Requirement: Show the location’s function and sensory pattern before a title card.
Implementation Note: Let players see post office + gas station + dance room before naming the village center.

Requirement: Each key scene should include at least three book-grounded details: one visual, one audio/sensory, one social/linguistic.
Implementation Note: Then add one original game-specific layer so the scene is transformed.

Requirement: No visual or musical ‘villain motif’ for faith. Show service, choir, ritual, tenderness, pressure, uncertainty, and disagreement.
Implementation Note: Abel’s interpretation is not the game’s definition of belief.

Requirement: Do not make players repeat abuse, chase perfect prevention, or earn bonuses for enduring harm.
Implementation Note: Safety options preserve the story and carry no shame penalty.

Requirement: When the player changes a journal conclusion, retain a trace of the earlier wording.
Implementation Note: Conflicting versions are gameplay, not errors to be instantly solved.

Requirement: Hospitals, courthouses, buses, dorms, and libraries should contain invisible rules and helpful people as well as friction.
Implementation Note: Avoid institution = salvation and family = ignorance binaries.

Requirement: Tools, vehicles, weather, animals, and repair methods must function plausibly.
Implementation Note: No ‘rustic aesthetic’ without task logic.

Requirement: Keep turn-of-the-millennium technology: dial-up, VCR cables, CB radio, early web, bulky camcorders, paper tests.
Implementation Note: No smartphones, modern GPS UI, or contemporary slang unless later acts require them.

Requirement: Background signs must use source-aware names or approved fictional analogues.
Implementation Note: Storefronts, road signs, lecture halls, and campus maps are narrative surfaces.

Requirement: NPCs should refer to prior shared events differently based on worldview and relationship state.
Implementation Note: The same accident may be ‘a miracle,’ ‘a shortcut,’ ‘bad luck,’ or ‘an unfiled incident.’

Requirement: UI communicates current intent and known risk, never ‘This will betray your family +10.’
Implementation Note: Behavior, access, tone, and later retellings carry consequence.

Requirement: Indigenous stories, Mormon history, disability, rural life, medical care, race, and international settings require specialist review.
Implementation Note: Source fidelity does not replace sensitivity or historical consultation.

Requirement: All new production uses Mara/Abel/Ruth/Jonah/Silas/Eliza/Nora/Caleb/Kline/Hale/Ortiz/Tess/Wade.
Implementation Note: Legacy names in old decks should be patched before voice recording or animatic timing.

Requirement: Every approved line, prop, sign, or landmark gets a chapter/page locator in the production database.
Implementation Note: This allows adaptation review, consistency checks, and legal review.
